(1) The props are typed. `Props` (line 5) declares `id: string`, `children?: ReactNode`, `className?: string`, `style?: CSSProperties` and `Icon?: LucideIcon`. Appear and SceneLayer type `children` as ReactNode. (2) Callers cannot override the identity hooks. Box, Label, Arrow, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip spread caller props first and then set `kind` (lines 7-12). Node does not spread caller props onto the element; it sets `layoutId={id}` and `data-presentation-node={kind}` itself (line 6). SceneLayer hardcodes `data-presentation-scene-layer` and takes only children. Since `Props` declares no data-presentation-* field, a caller cannot supply one. (3) Kit-only props stay off the DOM. Judges A and B voted fail because `Props` is a hand-written type rather than ComponentProps&lt;&#39;div&#39;&gt;/HTMLMotionProps, so callers cannot pass aria-*, data-* or event handlers. That observation is correct but does not decide the criterion. The requirement contrasts element-prop typing with &#39;an untyped bag such as Record&lt;string, unknown&gt;&#39;, and the review guidance fails a primitive only when it &#39;types its props as an untyped bag … instead of the rendered element&#39;s props&#39;. It also says &#39;Typed primitives that apply identity hooks after caller props and strip kit-only props pass.&#39; Nothing requires the primitives to accept every attribute of the element, and passing aria-* or event handlers is a scenario the guidance does not name. They do not take the rendered element&#39;s props (`HTMLMotionProps&lt;&#39;div&#39;&gt;` or `ComponentProps&lt;&#39;div&#39;&gt;`), so callers cannot pass ordinary element props such as `aria-*`, `data-*` or event handlers. Fix, or decision needed?"},{"line":1600,"text":""},{"line":1601,"text":"**Question.** The tester reproduced the reference sample at 390×844. The 880px canvas scales to 350px (factor 0.398), so 9px diagram labels render at about 3.6px. Title and caption stay legible, and there is no horizontal overflow. Should this be fixed in the sample, or is a user decision needed?"},{"line":1602,"text":""},{"line":1603,"text":"**Requirement.**"},{"line":1604,"text":"- \"Fixed-canvas fit scaling\" (`specs/evolving-scene-presentations/spec.md`): the diagram \"SHALL be composed in a fixed design canvas and scaled uniformly to fit the available viewport, so the composition does not reflow\". The default canvas is 880 × 380."},{"line":1605,"text":"- AT-003 expects \"important content remains readable without accidental chrome collisions at both viewport widths\"."},{"line":1606,"text":"- The sample's per-step visual design, including entity shapes, coordinates and colors, is deferred to design."},{"line":1607,"text":"- \"Entities accumulate; they are never rearranged or redrawn.\""},{"line":1608,"text":""},{"line":1609,"text":"**Ruling.** I made no code change. This is a decision needed from the user, not \"not a defect\". The tester's reading, that the narrow screenshot shows diagram text as unreadable marks, is accurate and a user would call it broken."},{"line":1610,"text":"- **Cause.** The fit is `(width − 40) / 880`, per the approved uniform-scaling requirement. At 390px that gives a factor of about 0.4. To render a label at roughly 10px, its design size would need to be about 25px."},{"line":1611,"text":"- **Why sample typography can't fix it.** The sample's text is 9–20px, set to fit five 143px cards and an 810px tray inside the 880 canvas. Raising the small labels to about 25px would overflow the cards. Raising them by 10–20% would still render at about 4–5px, so it would not resolve the finding."},{"line":1612,"text":"- **Why I did not make that small change.** It would add layout-collision risk (for example the \"visual →\" connector already abuts \"✳ EDITED\" at step 8). It would not remove the finding, so it would only add risk and the next round would still fail it."},{"line":1613,"text":"- **Options inside the approved definition.** None resolves it fully. The two bounded levers are the page padding, which would gain about 2% scale, and the sample's design canvas, which presentations may override. The sample would still need a layout that reads at a 350px-wide scale."},{"line":1614,"text":"- **Options that change an approved requirement.**"},{"line":1615,"text":" - (a) Narrow-viewport geometry, such as a separate design canvas or re-composition below some width. This conflicts with \"does not reflow\"."},{"line":1616,"text":" - (b) Horizontal pan or zoom on small screens. This is a new requirement."},{"line":1617,"text":" - (c) Accept uniform scaling as the specified behavior. Diagram text is then an overview at phone width, and AT-003's \"readable\" is read as title, caption and chrome. This is a clarification of the test plan's expected result."},{"line":1618,"text":""},{"line":1619,"text":"**Rationale.** Readability at 390px and unchanged uniform scaling of an 880px composition cannot both hold for this dense sample. Choosing between them changes an approved requirement or the test plan's expectation, which needs the user."},{"line":1620,"text":""},{"line":1621,"text":"**Pending decision from the user.** Choose (a), (b) or (c) above, or direct a redesign of the sample's composition for a smaller canvas. Until then F-001 stays open. No tracked file changed and no test was run for it."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-90c677c65c2d5196 (assumptions-ledger)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":1746,"end_line":1755,"lines":[{"line":1746,"text":"# Acceptance screenshots"},{"line":1747,"text":""},{"line":1748,"text":"All screenshots below were captured at revision `63cd8c77c378980e96ef6c9144305decba0a7bd2`. Fix, or decision needed?"},{"line":1600,"text":""},{"line":1601,"text":"**Question.** The tester reproduced the reference sample at 390×844. The 880px canvas scales to 350px (factor 0.398), so 9px diagram labels render at about 3.6px. Title and caption stay legible, and there is no horizontal overflow. Should this be fixed in the sample, or is a user decision needed?"},{"line":1602,"text":""},{"line":1603,"text":"**Requirement.**"},{"line":1604,"text":"- \"Fixed-canvas fit scaling\" (`specs/evolving-scene-presentations/spec.md`): the diagram \"SHALL be composed in a fixed design canvas and scaled uniformly to fit the available viewport, so the composition does not reflow\". The default canvas is 880 × 380."},{"line":1605,"text":"- AT-003 expects \"important content remains readable without accidental chrome collisions at both viewport widths\"."},{"line":1606,"text":"- The sample's per-step visual design, including entity shapes, coordinates and colors, is deferred to design."},{"line":1607,"text":"- \"Entities accumulate; they are never rearranged or redrawn.\""},{"line":1608,"text":""},{"line":1609,"text":"**Ruling.** I made no code change. This is a decision needed from the user, not \"not a defect\". The tester's reading, that the narrow screenshot shows diagram text as unreadable marks, is accurate and a user would call it broken."},{"line":1610,"text":"- **Cause.** The fit is `(width − 40) / 880`, per the approved uniform-scaling requirement. At 390px that gives a factor of about 0.4. To render a label at roughly 10px, its design size would need to be about 25px."},{"line":1611,"text":"- **Why sample typography can't fix it.** The sample's text is 9–20px, set to fit five 143px cards and an 810px tray inside the 880 canvas. Raising the small labels to about 25px would overflow the cards. Raising them by 10–20% would still render at about 4–5px, so it would not resolve the finding."},{"line":1612,"text":"- **Why I did not make that small change.** It would add layout-collision risk (for example the \"visual →\" connector already abuts \"✳ EDITED\" at step 8). It would not remove the finding, so it would only add risk and the next round would still fail it."},{"line":1613,"text":"- **Options inside the approved definition.** None resolves it fully. The two bounded levers are the page padding, which would gain about 2% scale, and the sample's design canvas, which presentations may override. The sample would still need a layout that reads at a 350px-wide scale."},{"line":1614,"text":"- **Options that change an approved requirement.**"},{"line":1615,"text":" - (a) Narrow-viewport geometry, such as a separate design canvas or re-composition below some width. This conflicts with \"does not reflow\"."},{"line":1616,"text":" - (b) Horizontal pan or zoom on small screens. This is a new requirement."},{"line":1617,"text":" - (c) Accept uniform scaling as the specified behavior. Diagram text is then an overview at phone width, and AT-003's \"readable\" is read as title, caption and chrome. This is a clarification of the test plan's expected result."},{"line":1618,"text":""},{"line":1619,"text":"**Rationale.** Readability at 390px and unchanged uniform scaling of an 880px composition cannot both hold for this dense sample. Choosing between them changes an approved requirement or the test plan's expectation, which needs the user."},{"line":1620,"text":""},{"line":1621,"text":"**Pending decision from the user.** Choose (a), (b) or (c) above, or direct a redesign of the sample's composition for a smaller canvas. Until then F-001 stays open. No tracked file changed and no test was run for it."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-90c677c65c2d5196 (assumptions-ledger)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":1746,"end_line":1755,"lines":[{"line":1746,"text":"# Acceptance screenshots"},{"line":1747,"text":""},{"line":1748,"text":"All screenshots below were captured at revision `63cd8c77c378980e96ef6c9144305decba0a7bd2`.
